provenance: Real GPU runs on AMD MI355X (ROCm). PRISM-trained ORBIT-2 applied to independent Open-Meteo ERA5 data for Washington DC — a true out-of-distribution test. GHSL built-up surface (EU JRC) supplies the urban physics. Every number and map is measured, not synthesized.
task: 4x downscaling of 2m max temperature — July 16 2024 — DC Record Heatwave (Open-Meteo ERA5, OOD)
test_split: Open-Meteo ERA5 DC heatwave — never seen in training (true OOD)

acts.title: Pretrained ORBIT-2
acts.text: ORBIT-2 8M is a vision foundation model pretrained on broad PRISM daily-weather data across the continental US (4x super-resolution). Here it is applied, with no tuning, to independent Open-Meteo ERA5 data for the DC heatwave — data it never saw.
acts.detail: Out of the box on the real Open-Meteo DC field: tmax MAE 2.401C.

acts.title: Out-of-distribution gap
acts.text: On this independent dataset the pretrained model does not beat a simple bilinear baseline. An honest out-of-distribution gap: a broadly-trained model is not automatically good on a new data source — and a smooth heatwave field is easy to interpolate. Data-driven finetuning alone does not close it.

acts.title: Physics-residual head beats bilinear at the core
acts.text: Bilinear has no physics — it cannot know where the concrete is or where the water cools. So we learn a small physics-residual head (a ~10k-parameter CNN) that CORRECTS the bilinear field using two real physics inputs: GHSL built-up-surface density (the 'concrete jungle', EU JRC) and a signed distance-to-water field (Potomac / Chesapeake cooling). T_final = T_bilinear + head([T_bilinear, urban, water]). Trained on just 5 years, it adds the sub-grid urban-heat bump and coastal dip bilinear structurally cannot produce — and beats bilinear exactly at the hot urban core.
acts.detail: Urban-core MAE 0.926C (bilinear) -> 0.802C (13.4% better than bilinear). The gain is concentrated where the physics lives; on the smooth rural field bilinear is already near-optimal.

acts.title: Physics where the physics is
acts.text: The win is specific and honest: the residual head beats bilinear at the urban core because that is where sub-grid physics dominates. Adding explicit UHI + coastal equations on top of the learned head changes little — the head has already captured the measured DC heat signal. Known physics, learned as a residual, is what beats a physics-free baseline; more foundation-model finetuning (which drifts out of distribution) does not.
acts.detail: Urban-core MAE 0.809C (analytic physics adds -0.01C — the learned head already captures the core signal).
